Subject: Re: Integration: SDK resilience & endpoint migration plan

Thanks Tessa — this looks great and aligned with what we want. A few quick notes from our side:

- FinEdge production traffic averages 1.2k RPS during peak and bursts to ~3k RPS for short periods.
- Current client infra sits behind an internal rate-shaping proxy; we can configure token-bucket there but would prefer your SDK defaults to be conservative.
- Procurement asked me to share the compliance window for firewall updates; they can do DNS changes only during business hours. Header-based routing is better for us.

Can you confirm the following:
1) Recommended steady-state client-side rate per instance (you suggested 20 rps — is that per worker thread or per host?)
2) For the canary steps, do you have a rollback threshold (error rate or latency) we should set to auto-fail the step?

I attached our internal network diagram and firewall maintenance note (attached).

—Hannah
Hannah Lee
Head of Integrations, FinEdge Labs

Attachment: finedge-network-diagram.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah@finedge.co>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procure@finedge.co>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration: SDK resilience & endpoint migration plan

Thanks — answers below.

1) "20 rps" recommendation is per SDK worker (per host-thread). If your client runs N workers, effective steady-state capacity per host = N * 20. If you use a single-threaded event loop, treat the limiter as per process. We recommend conservative defaults in the packaged SDK (20 rps, burst 50) and allowing customers to override via environment variable.

2) Rollback thresholds we recommend for each canary step (automated check at 15 minutes after cutover increment):
   - Error rate > 1.5% (5xx + 429) => rollback
   - 95th percentile latency increase > 50% vs baseline => rollback
   - Increase in client-side retry rate > 200% => investigate and pause

3) Additional server-side guardrails we will enforce for your account (already set in staging):
   - Per-route soft throttle at 2.5k rps, hard throttle at 3.5k rps (returns 429).
   - Route tagging for canary traffic so metrics are isolated (header X-Redwood-Canary: true).

Attached to this message is a compact runbook (finedge-integration-runbook.pdf) and an SDK samples tarball (sdk-samples.tar.gz) containing the Node/Python examples above plus a Go snippet that uses a leaky-bucket wrapper. I also added a basic Grafana dashboard link in the runbook.

Proposed canary timeline (local times):
- T+0:00 — 1% traffic (10m warmup, 15m observation)
- T+2h — 5% traffic (15m observation)
- T+6h — 20% traffic (30m observation)
- T+24h — 100% traffic (monitor for 24h)

If procurement needs DNS-only changes, we can still do the header-based rollout inside your network by configuring the internal proxy to add the X-Redwood-Canary header for selected requests.

Next step: Monica will pick up the implementation plan and coordinate a 2hr cutover window.

Thanks,
Tessa

Confirming final operational numbers for the runbook and who will page on alerts: 

- Client defaults: 20 rps per worker, burst 50, queue depth cap 200.
- Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 4 retries, initial 200ms.
- Server-side soft/hard throttle: 2.5k / 3.5k rps.
- Canary header: X-Redwood-Canary=true (will be injected by your proxy per Monica's schedule).
- Rollback automation: we will auto-fail a canary step if any rollback threshold triggers; an automated rollback will flip the header mapping back and notify the on-call.

On-call rotation for the window (Thu 2026-07-02 02:00–04:00 PST):
- Redwood infra on-call: Vivek Kulkarni (primary), Kimberly Park (secondary)
- FinEdge on-call: Hannah Lee (primary), Procure team as notified

I’ll add the Grafana panels and set Alerts: 95p latency > 50% increase, 5xx+429 rate > 1.5%, retry rate > 200% spike. Monica — please confirm the calendar invite and I’ll attach alert runbooks to it.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
